romaji: Massugu itte,
meaning: Go straight.
kana: まっすぐ行って
original:
すみません、本屋はどこですか？
Sumimasen, honya wa doko desu ka?
Excuse me, where is the bookstore? — Answer segment 1 of 3
grammar_note: Iku (to go) → itte, the irregular te-form. Here it links “go straight” to the following instruction; it is not past tense.

guide.forms: Iku (to go) → itte, the irregular te-form. Here it links “go straight” to the following instruction; it is not past tense.
guide.particles: Massugu describes how to go. No particle is needed between this adverb and itte.
guide.past: For a past statement, iku → itta: Massugu itta. = I went straight. The original is an instruction, not a past event.
guide.swap: Replace massugu with yukkuri: Yukkuri itte. = Go slowly. This card is the opening segment of the full answer.

romaji: Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatte kudasai.
meaning: Turn left at the second corner.
kana: 二つ目の角を左に曲がってください
original:
すみません、本屋はどこですか？
Sumimasen, honya wa doko desu ka?
Excuse me, where is the bookstore? — Answer segment 2 of 3
grammar_note: Magaru (u-verb, to turn) → magatte + kudasai = please turn. Futatsume means second.

guide.forms: Magaru (u-verb, to turn) → magatte + kudasai = please turn. Futatsume means second.
guide.particles: No links second and corner. O marks the corner where you turn; ni marks the direction, left.
guide.past: A request does not become a past request. To report the action: Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatta. = I turned left at the second corner.
guide.swap: Hidari → migi: Futatsume no kado o migi ni magatte kudasai. = Turn right at the second corner. Futatsume → hitotsume changes it to the first corner.

romaji: Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimasu yo.
meaning: The bookstore is on the left side of the street.
kana: 本屋は道の左側にありますよ
original:
すみません、本屋はどこですか？
Sumimasen, honya wa doko desu ka?
Excuse me, where is the bookstore? — Answer segment 3 of 3
grammar_note: Aru (u-verb, to exist) → arimasu, polite nonpast. Use aru for a place or inanimate thing, not iru.

guide.forms: Aru (u-verb, to exist) → arimasu, polite nonpast. Use aru for a place or inanimate thing, not iru.
guide.particles: Wa marks bookstore as topic; no links street to its left side; ni marks where it is; yo adds information for the listener.
guide.past: Arimasu → arimashita: Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimashita. = The bookstore was on the left side of the street.
guide.swap: Honya → ginkou and hidarigawa → migigawa: Ginkou wa michi no migigawa ni arimasu yo. = The bank is on the right side of the street.

romaji: Massugu itte, futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatte kudasai. Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimasu yo.
meaning: Go straight, turn left at the second corner. The bookstore is on the left side of the street.
kana: まっすぐ行って、二つ目の角を左に曲がってください。本屋は道の左側にありますよ。
original:
すみません、本屋はどこですか？
Sumimasen, honya wa doko desu ka?
prompt: Excuse me, where is the bookstore? Give the whole answer.
grammar_note: Put all three parts together: go straight, turn left at the second corner, then explain where the bookstore is.
requires: Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatte kudasai.
Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimasu yo.

guide.forms: Iku → itte connects the first instruction; magaru → magatte kudasai makes a polite request; aru → arimasu describes the bookstore location.
guide.particles: No links second to corner and street to left side. O marks the turning point; ni marks the turning direction and bookstore location. Wa marks the bookstore as topic; yo provides information.
guide.past: Instructions are requests, not past statements. To report the trip: Massugu itte, futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatta. Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimashita. = I went straight and turned left; the bookstore was on the left.
guide.swap: For a bank on the right, swap honya → ginkou, hidari → migi, and hidarigawa → migigawa. Keep the particles and sentence pattern.

romaji: Konnichiwa. Ogenki desu ka?
meaning: Hello. How are you?
kana: こんにちはお元気ですか
grammar_note: Ogenki desu ka asks how someone is doing.

guide.forms: Konnichiwa is a greeting; genki is a na-adjective. Desu makes the question polite.
guide.particles: O- is a polite prefix in ogenki; ka marks the question.
guide.past: Ogenki deshita ka? = Were you well? Konnichiwa has no tense.
guide.swap: Ogenki desu ka? → Oisogashii desu ka? = Are you busy? (Different adjective type; do not copy na-adjective rules onto isogashii.)

romaji: Toukyou no tenki wa dou desu ka?
meaning: How is the weather in Tokyo?
kana: 東京の天気はどうですか
grammar_note: No links Tokyo to its weather; dou desu ka asks what it is like.

guide.forms: Dou desu ka asks how something is. There is no action verb here.
guide.particles: No links Tokyo and its weather; wa marks the weather as topic; ka makes the question.
guide.past: Toukyou no tenki wa dou deshita ka? = How was the weather in Tokyo?
guide.swap: Toukyou → Oosaka: Oosaka no tenki wa dou desu ka?

romaji: San Furanshisuko no tenki wa yoi desu.
meaning: The weather in San Francisco is nice.
kana: サンフランシスコの天気はよいです
grammar_note: Yoi means good or nice. San Furanshisuko is written as two romaji words here.

guide.forms: Yoi is the standard form related to ii (good), an i-adjective.
guide.particles: No links the city and weather; wa marks the topic.
guide.past: Yoi → yokatta: San Furanshisuko no tenki wa yokatta desu. = The weather was nice. Desu stays desu with a past i-adjective.
guide.swap: Yoi → samui: San Furanshisuko no tenki wa samui desu. = The weather is cold.

romaji: Watashi ni wa chichi to haha to imouto ga hitori imasu.
meaning: I have a father, a mother, and one younger sister.
kana: 私には父と母といもうとが一人います
grammar_note: To joins family members; hitori counts one person. Imasu is the polite form of iru, used for people.

guide.forms: iru (ru-verb) → imasu: people exist / I have family members. Hitori means one person.
guide.particles: Ni wa presents your situation; to lists family; ga marks who exists. Hitori is intended to count the younger sister here.
guide.past: Imasu → imashita = I had / there were these family members. A past form can suggest a changed family situation, so use it only when intended.
guide.swap: Imouto ga hitori → imouto ga futari (two younger sisters). A clearer standalone count is Watashi ni wa imouto ga hitori imasu.

romaji: Chichi to haha wa Ookurando ni sunde imasu.
meaning: My father and mother live in Oakland.
kana: 父と母はオークランドに住んでいます
grammar_note: Sumu → sunde + imasu means live / reside. Ni marks where they live.

guide.forms: sumu (u-verb) → sunde + iru → sunde imasu: live / reside.
guide.particles: To joins father and mother; wa marks them as topic; ni marks residence.
guide.past: Sunde imasu → sunde imashita = lived / were living. The auxiliary iru changes tense; sunde stays the same.
guide.swap: Ookurando → Toukyou: Chichi to haha wa Toukyou ni sunde imasu.

romaji: Demo, imouto wa San Diego ni sunde imasu.
meaning: But my younger sister lives in San Diego.
kana: でもいもうとはサンディエゴに住んでいます
grammar_note: Demo means but. Sumu → sunde imasu describes where someone lives.

guide.forms: sumu → sunde imasu. Demo introduces a contrast.
guide.particles: Wa marks the younger sister; ni marks where she lives.
guide.past: Sunde imasu → sunde imashita = my younger sister lived there.
guide.swap: Imouto → ani: Demo, ani wa San Diego ni sunde imasu. = But my older brother lives in San Diego.

romaji: Chichi wa rokujussai desu.
meaning: My father is 60.
kana: 父はろくじゅっさいです
grammar_note: Rokujussai means sixty years old. Keep the doubled ss.

guide.forms: Rokujussai is an age expression, not a verb. Desu is the polite copula.
guide.particles: Wa marks father as the topic.
guide.past: Desu → deshita: Chichi wa rokujussai deshita. = My father was 60.
guide.swap: Rokujussai → gojussai: Chichi wa gojussai desu. = My father is 50.

romaji: Haha wa gojussai desu.
meaning: My mother is 50.
kana: 母は五十歳です
grammar_note: Gojussai means fifty years old.

guide.forms: Gojussai is an age expression; desu is the polite ending.
guide.particles: Wa marks mother as the topic.
guide.past: Haha wa gojussai deshita. = My mother was 50.
guide.swap: Gojussai → rokujussai: Haha wa rokujussai desu. = My mother is 60.

romaji: Imouto wa juuhassai desu.
meaning: My younger sister is 18.
kana: いもうとは十八歳です
grammar_note: Juuhassai means eighteen years old; hassai uses doubled ss.

guide.forms: Juuhassai means eighteen years old; desu links it to the topic.
guide.particles: Wa marks the younger sister.
guide.past: Imouto wa juuhassai deshita. = My younger sister was 18.
guide.swap: Juuhassai → juukyuusai: Imouto wa juukyuusai desu. = My younger sister is 19.

romaji: Chichi wa kensetsu no shigoto o shite imasu.
meaning: My father works in construction.
kana: 父はけんせつのしごとをしています
grammar_note: Suru → shite + imasu describes an occupation. Kensetsu no shigoto means construction work.

guide.forms: suru → shite + iru → shite imasu: doing work / working in an occupation.
guide.particles: Wa marks father; no describes the kind of work; o marks shigoto as the object of suru.
guide.past: Shite imasu → shite imashita = worked / was working. Change the final auxiliary, not shite.
guide.swap: Kensetsu → jimu: Chichi wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu. = My father does office work.

romaji: Haha wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu.
meaning: My mother does office work.
kana: 母はじむのしごとをしています
grammar_note: Jimu means office / administrative work here. Shite imasu comes from suru, to do.

guide.forms: suru → shite imasu. Jimu here means office administration, not the gym (jimu in katakana).
guide.particles: Wa marks mother; no connects office work to shigoto; o marks the object.
guide.past: Shite imasu → shite imashita = my mother did office work.
guide.swap: Haha → ani: Ani wa jimu no shigoto o shite imasu.

romaji: Imouto wa daigakusei desu.
meaning: My younger sister is a college student.
kana: いもうとは大学生です
grammar_note: Daigakusei means college student.

guide.forms: Daigakusei is a noun. Desu is the polite copula; plain form is da.
guide.particles: Wa marks the younger sister as topic.
guide.past: Desu → deshita: Imouto wa daigakusei deshita. = My younger sister was a college student.
guide.swap: Daigakusei → kaishain: Imouto wa kaishain desu. = My younger sister is a company employee.

romaji: Chichi to terebi o mimasu.
meaning: I watch TV with my father.
kana: 父とテレビを見ます
grammar_note: To means with; miru → mimasu means watch (polite).

guide.forms: miru (ru-verb) → mimasu: drop ru and add masu.
guide.particles: To means with father; o marks TV as what you watch. The subject I is understood.
guide.past: Mimasu → mimashita (polite); miru → mita (plain). Chichi to terebi o mimashita. = I watched TV with my father.
guide.swap: Terebi → eiga: Chichi to eiga o mimasu. = I watch a movie with my father.

romaji: Haha to haikingu ni ikimasu.
meaning: I go hiking with my mother.
kana: 母とハイキングに行きます
grammar_note: Iku → ikimasu means go (polite). Haikingu ni iku means go hiking.

guide.forms: iku (u-verb) → ikimasu. Haikingu ni iku is go hiking.
guide.particles: To marks mother as companion; ni marks the activity you go to do.
guide.past: Ikimasu → ikimashita (polite); iku → itta (irregular plain past).
guide.swap: Haha → tomodachi: Tomodachi to haikingu ni ikimasu. = I go hiking with friends.

romaji: Imouto to geemu o shimasu.
meaning: I play games with my younger sister.
kana: いもうととゲームをします
grammar_note: Suru → shimasu means do (polite). Geemu o suru means play games.

guide.forms: suru (irregular) → shimasu: do / play.
guide.particles: The first to follows imouto (with my sister); o marks games as the object.
guide.past: Shimasu → shimashita (polite); suru → shita (plain).
guide.swap: Geemu → tenisu: Imouto to tenisu o shimasu. = I play tennis with my younger sister.

romaji: Sore dewa, minasan ni oai suru no o tanoshimi ni shite imasu.
meaning: I look forward to meeting you all.
kana: それでは皆さんにお会いするのを楽しみにしています
grammar_note: Oai suru is a polite expression for meeting. No makes meeting you all into a noun phrase. Tanoshimi ni shite imasu means look forward to.

guide.forms: au → oai suru is a humble expression for meeting. Suru stays nonpast before no; shite imasu comes from suru + iru.
guide.particles: Ni marks whom you meet; no turns meeting into a noun phrase; o marks what you look forward to; ni belongs to tanoshimi ni suru.
guide.past: Final shite imasu → shite imashita = I was looking forward to meeting you all. Keep oai suru unchanged because the meeting was still anticipated at that time.
guide.swap: Minasan → sensei: Sensei ni oai suru no o tanoshimi ni shite imasu. = I look forward to meeting the teacher.

romaji: Yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
meaning: Thank you in advance.
kana: よろしくお願いします
grammar_note: A polite closing requesting goodwill; the English translation depends on context.

guide.forms: Onegai suru → onegai shimasu: a set polite request / closing, not a literal universal “thank you.”
guide.particles: No standalone particles occur in this expression. Yoroshiku modifies the request.
guide.past: Do not mechanically turn this greeting into a past-tense closing. Onegai shimashita means “I asked / requested,” a different statement.
guide.swap: For a more formal closing: Yoroshiku onegai itashimasu. Keep the set phrase intact.

romaji: Arekkusu yori
meaning: From Alex
kana: アレックスより
grammar_note: Yori means from in a letter signature.

guide.forms: A signature fragment, not a verb sentence; there is no dictionary verb to conjugate.
guide.particles: Yori means from and follows the sender’s name.
guide.past: No tense change: a name + yori signature is the same in a letter about past or present events.
guide.swap: Arekkusu → Mearii: Mearii yori = From Mary.

romaji: Watashi wa taitei asa hachiji goro okiru.
meaning: I usually wake up around 8 a.m.
kana: 私はたいてい朝八時ごろ起きる
grammar_note: Okiru is a ru-verb in its dictionary / plain nonpast form. Here it describes a routine, not a past event.

guide.forms: okiru (ru-verb) stays plain nonpast to describe a routine.
guide.particles: Wa marks the speaker; goro means around and follows the time.
guide.past: Okiru → okita (plain) / okimashita (polite).
guide.swap: Hachiji → shichiji: Asa shichiji goro okiru. = I wake around 7 a.m.

romaji: Sorekara, tsumetai shawaa o abite, asagohan o tabete, basu de shigoto ni iku.
meaning: Then I take a cold shower, eat breakfast, and go to work by bus.
kana: それから冷たいシャワーを浴びて朝ご飯を食べてバスで仕事に行く
grammar_note: Abiru → abite; taberu → tabete: te-forms link actions. Iku at the end sets the nonpast tense of the sequence.

guide.forms: abiru → abite; taberu → tabete (ru-verbs). Iku ends the sequence.
guide.particles: O marks shower and breakfast; de marks transport; ni marks destination.
guide.past: Change final iku → itta: abite and tabete stay in te-form. The whole sequence is then past.
guide.swap: Basu de → densha de (by train); shigoto ni → gakkou ni (to school).

romaji: Gogo wa konpyuutaa de muzukashii mondai o toku.
meaning: In the afternoon, I solve difficult problems on the computer.
kana: 午後はコンピューターで難しい問題を解く
grammar_note: Toku means solve; it is a u-verb. De marks the tool, the computer; o marks the problems being solved.

guide.forms: toku (u-verb) means solve; not to talk.
guide.particles: Wa marks afternoon as topic; de marks the computer as tool; o marks problems.
guide.past: Toku → toita (plain) / tokimashita (polite).
guide.swap: Muzukashii → yasashii (easy): yasashii mondai o toku = solve easy problems.

romaji: Shigoto wa isogashikute taihen da.
meaning: Work is busy and tough.
kana: 仕事は忙しくて大変だ
grammar_note: Isogashii → isogashikute joins an i-adjective to another description. Taihen is a na-adjective; da is the plain ending.

guide.forms: isogashii → isogashikute joins descriptions; taihen is a na-adjective.
guide.particles: Wa marks work as topic.
guide.past: Change final da → datta: Shigoto wa isogashikute taihen datta. = Work was busy and tough.
guide.swap: Shigoto → gakkou: Gakkou wa isogashikute taihen da. = School is busy and tough.

romaji: Sorekara, tomodachi to koohii o nomi ni itte, kyuukei suru.
meaning: Then I go drink coffee with friends and take a break.
kana: それから友達とコーヒーを飲みに行って休憩する
grammar_note: Nomu → nomimasu → nomi (stem) + ni expresses purpose. Iku → itte links going to kyuukei suru, taking a break.

guide.forms: nomu → nomimasu → nomi (stem); iku → itte; kyuukei suru = take a break.
guide.particles: To marks friends as companions; o marks coffee; stem + ni gives the purpose of going.
guide.past: Change final suru → shita; itte remains te-form.
guide.swap: Koohii → ocha: ocha o nomi ni iku = go to drink tea.

romaji: Koohii wa tsumetakute oishii.
meaning: The coffee is cold and delicious.
kana: コーヒーは冷たくておいしい
grammar_note: Tsumetai → tsumetakute joins two descriptions. The final adjective oishii sets the tense.

guide.forms: tsumetai → tsumetakute joins descriptions; oishii stays nonpast.
guide.particles: Wa marks coffee as topic.
guide.past: Oishii → oishikatta: Koohii wa tsumetakute oishikatta. = The coffee was cold and delicious.
guide.swap: Tsumetakute → atatakakute: Koohii wa atatakakute oishii. = The coffee is warm and delicious.

romaji: Gogo goji made ni ie ni kaeru.
meaning: I return home by 5 p.m.
kana: 午後五時までに家に帰る
grammar_note: Made ni means by a deadline; ni after ie marks the destination. Kaeru is a u-verb despite ending in eru.

guide.forms: kaeru (u-verb) means return; do not treat it as a ru-verb.
guide.particles: Made ni marks the deadline; ie ni marks home as destination.
guide.past: Kaeru → kaetta (plain) / kaerimashita (polite).
guide.swap: Goji → rokuji: Gogo rokuji made ni ie ni kaeru. = I return home by 6 p.m.

romaji: Soshite, atatakai bangohan o tabete, tomodachi to tanoshii terebi geemu o suru.
meaning: Then I eat a warm dinner and play fun video games with friends.
kana: そして温かい晩ご飯を食べて友達と楽しいテレビゲームをする
grammar_note: Taberu → tabete links eating to playing. To marks companions; o marks the object of each activity.

guide.forms: taberu → tabete; suru ends the linked sequence.
guide.particles: O marks dinner and games; to marks friends as companions.
guide.past: Change final suru → shita; tabete remains te-form.
guide.swap: Tomodachi to → imouto to: play with your younger sister instead.

romaji: Demo, watashitachi wa geemu ga amari jouzu janai.
meaning: But we aren’t very good at games.
kana: でも私たちはゲームがあまり上手じゃない
grammar_note: Amari pairs with a negative: not very. Jouzu is a na-adjective; jouzu janai means not good at.

guide.forms: jouzu is a na-adjective; janai is its plain negative.
guide.particles: Wa marks we; ga marks games as the skill; amari plus negative means not very.
guide.past: Janai → janakatta: Geemu ga amari jouzu janakatta. = We were not very good at games.
guide.swap: Geemu → tenisu: Watashitachi wa tenisu ga amari jouzu janai.

romaji: Shuumatsu wa jimu ni iku.
meaning: On weekends, I go to the gym.
kana: 週末はジムに行く
grammar_note: Wa presents weekends as the time topic. Ni marks the destination; iku is plain nonpast.

guide.forms: iku is plain nonpast, describing a weekend habit.
guide.particles: Wa marks weekends as time topic; ni marks gym as destination.
guide.past: Iku → itta: Shuumatsu wa jimu ni itta. = I went to the gym on the weekend.
guide.swap: Jimu → toshokan: Shuumatsu wa toshokan ni iku. = I go to the library on weekends.

romaji: Sorekara, tomodachi to asobu.
meaning: Then I hang out with friends.
kana: それから友達と遊ぶ
grammar_note: To marks who you spend time with. Asobu is a u-verb meaning play / hang out.

guide.forms: asobu (u-verb) means play / spend leisure time.
guide.particles: To marks the companion.
guide.past: Asobu → asonda (plain) / asobimashita (polite).
guide.swap: Tomodachi → imouto: Sorekara, imouto to asobu. = Then I hang out with my younger sister.

romaji: Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga suki desu.
meaning: I like driving.
kana: わたしはくるまをうんてんするのがすきです
grammar_note: Unten suru means drive. Suru stays in dictionary form before no. Suki is a na-adjective, not a verb.

guide.forms: Unten suru means drive. Suru stays in dictionary form before no. Suki is a na-adjective, not a verb.
guide.particles: Wa marks you as topic; o marks the car; no turns driving into an activity noun; ga marks what you like.
guide.past: Suki desu → suki deshita = I liked driving. Keep unten suru unchanged for the general activity.
guide.swap: Kuruma o unten suru → hon o yomu: Watashi wa hon o yomu no ga suki desu. = I like reading books.

romaji: Watashi wa itsumo kuruma o unten shimasu.
meaning: I always drive.
kana: わたしはいつもくるまをうんてんします
grammar_note: Unten suru → unten shimasu: polite nonpast. Itsumo means always.

guide.forms: Unten suru → unten shimasu: polite nonpast. Itsumo means always.
guide.particles: Wa marks you as topic; o marks the car being driven.
guide.past: Shimasu → shimashita: Watashi wa itsumo kuruma o unten shimashita. = I always drove (in the period being discussed).
guide.swap: Itsumo → tokidoki: Watashi wa tokidoki kuruma o unten shimasu. = I sometimes drive.

romaji: Unten wa tanoshikute omoshiroi to omoimasu.
meaning: I think driving is fun and interesting.
kana: うんてんはたのしくておもしろいとおもいます
grammar_note: Tanoshii → tanoshikute links two descriptions. Omou → omoimasu means think (polite).

guide.forms: Tanoshii → tanoshikute links two descriptions. Omou → omoimasu means think (polite).
guide.particles: Wa marks driving; to marks the thought: fun and interesting.
guide.past: Omoimasu → omoimashita = I thought driving was fun and interesting. To describe driving itself as past while keeping “I think,” use tanoshikute omoshirokatta to omoimasu.
guide.swap: Unten → ryouri: Ryouri wa tanoshikute omoshiroi to omoimasu. = I think cooking is fun and interesting.

romaji: Watashi wa shashin o toru no ga kirai desu. Muzukashii kara desu.
meaning: I dislike taking photos because it’s difficult.
kana: わたしはしゃしんをとるのがきらいですむずかしいからです
grammar_note: Toru (u-verb) means take a photo; it stays in dictionary form before no. Kirai is a na-adjective. Muzukashii is an i-adjective.

guide.forms: Toru (u-verb) means take a photo; it stays in dictionary form before no. Kirai is a na-adjective. Muzukashii is an i-adjective.
guide.particles: O marks photos; no turns taking photos into an activity; ga marks what you dislike; kara explains the reason.
guide.past: Kirai desu → kirai deshita; muzukashii → muzukashikatta: I disliked taking photos because it was difficult. Keep toru nonpast for the general activity.
guide.swap: Shashin o toru → oyogu: Watashi wa oyogu no ga kirai desu. Muzukashii kara desu. = I dislike swimming because it is difficult.

romaji: Sorekara, watashi wa ryouri o suru no ga jouzu desu. Omoshiroi to omou kara desu.
meaning: Then, I’m good at cooking because I find it interesting.
kana: それからわたしはりょうりをするのがじょうずですおもしろいとおもうからです
grammar_note: Suru stays in dictionary form before no. Jouzu is a na-adjective. Omou stays plain before kara, even though the sentence ends politely.

guide.forms: Suru stays in dictionary form before no. Jouzu is a na-adjective. Omou stays plain before kara, even though the sentence ends politely.
guide.particles: O marks cooking; no makes the activity a noun phrase; ga marks the skill; to marks the thought; kara means because.
guide.past: Jouzu desu → jouzu deshita; omou → omotta: Omoshiroi to omotta kara desu = because I thought it was interesting. Do not automatically make every embedded word past.
guide.swap: Ryouri o suru → e o kaku: Watashi wa e o kaku no ga jouzu desu. = I am good at drawing. Use this as a pattern; praising your own skill with jouzu can sound boastful in conversation.

romaji: Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga heta desu. Amari renshuu shinai kara desu.
meaning: I’m bad at sports because I don’t practice much.
kana: わたしはスポーツをするのがへたですあまりれんしゅうしないからです
grammar_note: Suru stays unchanged before no. Renshuu suru → renshuu shinai is the plain negative of practice. Heta is a na-adjective.

guide.forms: Suru stays unchanged before no. Renshuu suru → renshuu shinai is the plain negative of practice. Heta is a na-adjective.
guide.particles: O marks sports; no makes doing sports an activity; ga marks the skill. Amari pairs with a negative for not much; kara gives the reason.
guide.past: Heta desu → heta deshita; shinai → shinakatta: Amari renshuu shinakatta kara desu = because I did not practice much.
guide.swap: Supootsu o suru → uta o utau: Watashi wa uta o utau no ga heta desu. = I am bad at singing.

romaji: Motto renshuu shimasu.
meaning: I will practice more.
kana: もっとれんしゅうします
grammar_note: Renshuu suru → renshuu shimasu. Polite nonpast can express future intention; motto means more.

guide.forms: Renshuu suru → renshuu shimasu. Polite nonpast can express future intention; motto means more.
guide.particles: No explicit particle is needed in this suru-verb phrase. The subject I is understood.
guide.past: Shimasu → shimashita: Motto renshuu shimashita. = I practiced more.
guide.swap: Renshuu → benkyou: Motto benkyou shimasu. = I will study more.

romaji: Kuroi shatsu o kite imasu.
meaning: I’m wearing a black shirt.
kana: くろいシャツをきています
grammar_note: Kiru (ru-verb, to put on upper-body clothing) → kite + imasu. The resulting state is “am wearing.” Kuroi is an i-adjective.

guide.forms: Kiru (ru-verb, to put on upper-body clothing) → kite + imasu. The resulting state is “am wearing.” Kuroi is an i-adjective.
guide.particles: O marks the shirt being worn. The subject I is understood.
guide.past: Kite imasu → kite imashita = I was wearing a black shirt. Keep kite unchanged.
guide.swap: Kuroi → shiroi: Shiroi shatsu o kite imasu. = I am wearing a white shirt.

romaji: Kuroi zubon o haite imasu.
meaning: I’m wearing black pants.
kana: くろいズボンをはいています
grammar_note: Haku (u-verb, to put on lower-body clothing or footwear) → haite + imasu = am wearing. Ku → ite makes the te-form.

guide.forms: Haku (u-verb, to put on lower-body clothing or footwear) → haite + imasu = am wearing. Ku → ite makes the te-form.
guide.particles: O marks the pants. Kuroi directly describes zubon; no na is needed.
guide.past: Haite imasu → haite imashita = I was wearing black pants.
guide.swap: Kuroi → aoi: Aoi zubon o haite imasu. = I am wearing blue pants.

romaji: Chairoi kutsu o haite imasu.
meaning: I’m wearing brown shoes.
kana: ちゃいろいくつをはいています
grammar_note: Haku → haite imasu is used for shoes as well as pants. Chairoi means brown and is an i-adjective.

guide.forms: Haku → haite imasu is used for shoes as well as pants. Chairoi means brown and is an i-adjective.
guide.particles: O marks shoes as the item worn. The subject I is understood.
guide.past: Haite imasu → haite imashita = I was wearing brown shoes.
guide.swap: Chairoi → kuroi: Kuroi kutsu o haite imasu. = I am wearing black shoes.

romaji: Kami ga mijikakute, se ga takai desu.
meaning: My hair is short, and I’m tall.
kana: かみがみじかくてせがたかいです
grammar_note: Mijikai → mijikakute links “hair is short” to the next description. Se ga takai literally means height is high. Both are i-adjectives.

guide.forms: Mijikai → mijikakute links “hair is short” to the next description. Se ga takai literally means height is high. Both are i-adjectives.
guide.particles: The first ga marks hair as the subject of short; the second ga marks height as the subject of high. My is understood from context.
guide.past: Change final takai → takakatta: Kami ga mijikakute, se ga takakatta desu. = My hair was short and I was tall. Desu stays desu after the past i-adjective.
guide.swap: Mijikakute → nagakute: Kami ga nagakute, se ga takai desu. = My hair is long and I am tall.
